summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for symptomatic in-stent restenosis of the right transplanted renal artery, presenting with elevated blood pressure. Ultrasound confirmed increased renal artery velocities. The patient underwent elective balloon angioplasty of the stenotic segment via right femoral access, with successful restoration of blood flow and no procedural complications. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with preserved renal function post-procedure. Pain was controlled, and he tolerated diet and ambulation well. He was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy, antihypertensives, immunosuppressants, and insulin, with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up with vascular surgery and transplant nephrology.
